items.title: Roy Palmer Interview, 1955-09-22
items.q: And they had another fellow that I played with, Joe Petit, named Yank Johnson.

ctx.x: Yeah, I didn't get to meet him. He died about two or three years ago. Yeah, George Field. I went to his house a couple of times here. Once talked to a niece. Uh-huh. He was over at the Union playing cards that afternoon. Yeah. Before I ever got back, he was dead then. Yeah. He was very good.

Very good. Nice trombone player. I used to see him play in marches. I was rather young then when he used to play in those bands, you know. Before I got down with bands, I saw him playing in that. And they'd play marches, you know, and things like that. He was a nice trombone player. That's what I learned. And I found out that playing trombone, when you're playing and making those smears, you know, and te-de-de-de-da-da, and following up to the other instrument, I paid attention to him, watched him closely on a…

Oh, yeah. Oh, Lord. One time I made a record of him, honey, was so old that he could hardly play. He played the sound without any teeth, no false teeth. He played both? He played just on the ground, not so well. No. The trouble was this. He was quite deaf. He could hardly hear. And one number they started out, he couldn't even hear what key they were playing in. Oh, I see. He started in the wrong key. Then when he found out what key it was, he heard it finally and changed. Yeah. But he made a couple of numbers…
